platform_scope: Windows + NTFS only. Hidden behavioural suite: verifier/tests/test_wsparse_semantics.py.

conditions.statement: preallocate() sets FSCTL_SET_SPARSE and moves the end-of-file marker instead of writing the tail out, so a 1 GiB reservation occupies less than 8 MiB and the file is reported as sparse by fsutil.
disk_usage() reports the cluster-aligned allocation of the file, not its logical length.
allocated_ranges() enumerates the byte ranges that are really backed by clusters, ascending and disjoint, inside the logical length.

sparse_flag(path, True) really sets the attribute, and setting it on an already dense file does not release the clusters that are already allocated (MS-FSCC: currently allocated clusters SHOULD NOT be deallocated).
conditions.windows_mechanism: DeviceIoControl(FSCTL_SET_SPARSE) + FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SPARSE_FILE, verified externally with fsutil sparse queryflag

conditions.statement: An object that cannot carry the sparse attribute (a directory) is reported as WSParseError(kind='unsupported'); an unusable argument is reported as kind='badarg'.
conditions.windows_mechanism: FSCTL_SET_SPARSE on a directory handle returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87)

conditions.statement: The reserved tail still reads back as zeros, the visible smoke suite keeps passing, and the public API keeps its names and signatures.
conditions.windows_mechanism: SetEndOfFile leaves the extended region as a hole that reads as zero bytes
